free_tier.stated: Basic: Free base plan, included disk 10 GiB, runtime limit 1 hour on the pricing page; the billing documentation states 24 hour max runtime and 20 concurrent sandboxes. Runtime and retained storage are billed separately in both.
free_tier.notes: The free part is a zero-cost team plan with a 10 GiB root disk; the plan carries no free runtime allowance. A positive prepaid balance is required before a sandbox can be created, and runtime is charged per second from €0.000020/vCPU-second and €0.000004/GiB-second. The pricing page says runtime limit 1 hour while the billing docs say 24 hour max runtime for Basic; the discrepancy is recorded in an open question.

per_object_cap.stated: Basic teams get a 10 GiB root disk; self-service sandbox resources use CPU of 1, 2, 4, 6 or 8 vCPU and memory from 512 MiB to 8192 MiB in 512 MiB increments.
per_object_cap.notes: The 10 GiB is the plan-managed root disk, not a single uploaded object cap; no maximum object size is published.

retention.stated: Inactive sandbox disks expire after seven days. This includes paused, stopped, failed, and lost sandboxes. Checkpoint expiry defaults to 24 hours after creation.
retention.notes: Resuming ends the seven-day window; a later stop starts a new one. Named persistent volumes and reusable template versions are not subject to this expiry.

egress.terms: No. Bandwidth is included with your plan, sized to match — normal app traffic at any tier isn't metered, shaped, or invoiced per GB. Sandbox egress is controlled by allow_internet_access, allow_package_registry_access, allow_out and deny_out policies.
egress.free_allowance: unlimited: bandwidth is included, no GB allowance published

interface_detail: Sandbox APIs live under https://api.watasu.io/v1 and use a Watasu API key as a bearer token; the data plane accepts file and streaming process operations at the route-token hostname. The SSH front door creates a sandbox from a template and opens a shell, and the watasu CLI wraps API keys for login.
tooling: Install the watasu CLI or call the REST API with a Watasu API key; an SSH front door creates a sandbox from a template and opens a shell, and SDKs use the data-plane URL plus a short-lived access token.
chaining: A sandbox runs an agent task with configurable egress allowlists, writes results to the retained 10 GiB disk or a named checkpoint, and uses the attached S3-compatible object storage add-on for data that must outlive the 7-day disk expiry.

limits.value: Basic: 10 GiB included root disk, 20 concurrent sandboxes, 24 hour max runtime per billing docs (pricing page states 1 hour runtime limit)
inactive sandbox disks expire after seven days; checkpoint expiry defaults to 24 hours
sandbox create and runtime mutation endpoints are rate-limited per authenticated user and remote address; 429 rate_limited with Retry-After (Basic create rate 1/second in the quota example)

limits_note: Balance must be greater than zero before create, checkpoint restore or resume; otherwise 402 sandbox_balance_required. Runtime, stopped disk (€0.10/GiB-month), checkpoints (€0.03/GiB-month) and templates (€0.03/GiB-month) bill separately. Pro plan is €150/mo base with 20 GiB disk, 100 concurrent sandboxes and 5 creates/sec.
binding_note: The Basic plan's 10 GiB root disk and 20 concurrent sandbox ceiling are reached before any per-second runtime charge becomes material; the example 2 vCPU + 1 GiB run costs about €0.1584/hour.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up page asks for Your name, Work email, Password and Confirm password; no phone number and no card are required to register. A saved payment card is not required, but the team billing account must have a balance greater than zero before creating a sandbox; card top-ups start at €5.

reliability_note: Inactive disks expire after seven days and checkpoints default to 24 hours; runaway spend is bounded by a prepaid balance and by build deadlines, and apps pause rather than accrue a surprise bill when the balance runs out.
confidence_note: The published EUR rates, free Basic plan, entitlement page, sign-up fields and egress answer are quoted from the vendor's pricing page and billing docs, all read 2026-11-24. The 1-hour versus 24-hour runtime discrepancy is documented in the evidence, not resolved.
